reasoning: Both attempts cover inputs and controller navigation well. B passes every check, uses fixed text sizes, shows a count of 0 as a number, and has a visible pressed state. A uses TextScaled on its tile labels, shows 'None yet' instead of 0, and fails StyLua. A's tie-in to the Vide scope for its connections is better, but that does not outweigh B's advantages.

criteria.criterion: Every action works with every input
criteria.note: Tiles, backdrop, close and open buttons all use Activated; B key and gamepad Y toggle through ContextActionService; the doc tables match the code.

Opening calls moveCursorToSelectedBlock, setting GuiService.SelectedObject; the Grid ScrollingFrame has SelectionGroup with Stop on all four sides; ButtonB is bound while open, with a fallback when SelectedObject is cleared.
84 px open button at bottom centre, 56 px close button, tiles at least 88-96 px, CoreUISafeInsets; bottom centre sits between the thumbstick and jump corners.
Locked tiles show 🔒 and 'Level N', and pressing one shows a footer message; but a count of 0 shows as 'None yet' instead of a number.
Name, count and lock are all on the tile; hover and gamepad focus share one outline. The selected block has a green stroke and tick, but there is no distinct pressed state on tiles.
Tile name, status and message labels use TextScaled with MinTextSize 12, against the rubric's fixed size per role; contrast on the dark panel is good.
A revision source bumped on BlockInventory.Changed, a BlockTypeChanged connection, and both wrapped in cleanup(); everything that changes is bound.
Works as described, but StyLua fails on InventoryApp.luau and selene gives fromOffset/fromScale warnings; the BlockPlacer number-key change is reasonable.

criteria.criterion: Every action works with every input
criteria.note: Tiles and the HUD button use Activated; B and ButtonY are bound to Toggle; the doc's tables cover every action on touch, mouse and keyboard, and controller.

The doc and checks confirm GuiService selection, a SelectionGroup set to Stop, and B bound at high priority with a fallback; SelectionOrder also puts the selected tile first. The panel code was cut off, so this is partly from the notes.
80 px button at top right below the top bar on touch, 96-120 px tiles, 48 px close button, CoreUISafeInsets; fitScale can shrink the panel to 0.5 on tiny screens.
Shows 🔒 and 'Level N' and a count of '0'; a refused pick shakes the tile and the details line explains why.
Everything is on the tile; hover details also show on focus and tap; pressed state (darker plus 2 px sink) and selected state (outline plus check badge) are both visible.
Fixed TextSize per role from TileMetrics (16-20 px), no TextScaled, light text on a dark panel.
InventoryState rebuilds entries on Changed and follows BlockTypeChanged; but those connections are module-level and never cleaned up with a Vide scope.
luau-lsp, selene and StyLua all pass; BlockPlacer is untouched; the doc honestly lists known gaps.

strengths: Thorough controller handling: initial selection, SelectionGroup, B to close plus a fallback
Placement is disabled while the screen is open, and Modal frees the mouse
Number keys follow the same canBuildWith rule as the screen
weaknesses: A count of 0 shows as 'None yet' rather than a number
Fails StyLua formatting, with selene style warnings

strengths: Fixed text sizes and a real pressed state
Respects reduced motion and the player's transparency setting, and has a compact phone layout
weaknesses: Signal connections live at module level and are not tied to the Vide scope
Fit scaling can shrink tiles below a comfortable size on very small screens
More complex than needed (a Screen module and many stories)
